newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen needs to clear 115 hurdle soon.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen needs to clear 115 hurdle soon.

text.p: The dollar's rally versus the Japanese currency remains on track but continued failure to breech the crucial 115 yen level puts the U.S. unit at risk of a pullback, chartists said.
"I'm still bullish on dollar/yen," said Ken Boyer, a technical analyst at MMS International. "We're still in an uptrend and the market hasn't signaled a reversal in that trend yet."
Boyer sketched good, intraday support for the dollar at 113.30 yen, Monday's low, and predicted the U.S. currency could recover to around 114.50 on an intraday basis.
Boyer also deemed 115 yen as the dollar's obvious short-term target.
The dollar came within striking distance of 115 yen in Asian trade on Tuesday when it hit 114.88 yen, its highest level since April 1993.
But by the afternoon in New York, the U.S. unit traded around 114.26/31 yen, up from 113.70/80 yen at the open.
I.D.E.A. Inc technical analyst Ben Morden also affirmed the dollar/yen rally.
"It's in a trend (and) you have to respect it," said Morden, adding the mark/yen rally will keep dollar/yen going.
Still, Morden said a dip below 75 in mark/yen or 113 in dollar/yen really undermines the rally on a multi-day basis.
He also warned there is more risk being long dollar/yen because the dollar is going to be due for a correction if it does not start building above 115 yen very soon.
"You have to be careful more with dollar/yen at this point because you got your correction in dollar/mark (already)," Morden said.
The dollar stood little changed in afternoon dealings versus the German currency, trading around 1.5100/05 marks compared with 1.5090/00 at the open.
Boyer noted the dollar triggered a downside correction when it broke below 1.53 marks early last week.
He said follow-through on that correction leaves the dollar targeting 1.5050 marks, which represents good chart support.
